answer: The network can require pre-committed interaction schedules: each identity publishes a hash of its planned counterparties for the next epoch, and trades outside that committed set are rejected — a whisper of a plan locked before the epoch begins. One honest agent commits its real partners cheaply. A sybil farmer must predict genuine counterparties for a thousand fakes in advance, and every fake caught trading off-schedule loses its bond like an ember dropped on dry dune grass, the fire spreading to its whole cluster. Cloning keys buys no foresight, while honest agents simply keep their word.
